newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: KLM says not in govt stake sale talks.
newsitem.headline: KLM says not in govt stake sale talks.

text.p: KLM Royal Dutch Airlines on Saturday denied a report in the Volkskrant daily newspaper that it was in talks with the Dutch government about the sale of the state's 38.2 percent stake in the airline.
"There are no talks with KLM and the government regarding the sell-off of these shares," a spokesman said.

KLM's 1995/96 annual report shows the government has 25.7 million common shares, 11.8 million A-cumulative preference shares and 1,300 priority shares, giving it a 38.2 percent voting interest in KLM. The government's majority holding went below 50 percent after a share issue in the 1970s, he said.

De Volkskrant said the government could raise around 1.4 billion guilders through the sale of its stake, based on the airline's current share price and said that KLM was considering whether to buy back some of the government's shares.
"They (reporters) asked me whether there are talks between KLM and the government regarding the sale of shares and the answer was 'definitely not'," the spokesman said.

Asked whether KLM had any plans to talk to the government about its shares he said: "At the moment there is no issue regarding this at KLM. It is not a subject of debate at KLM." KLM's shares closed up 0.90 guilder on Friday at 41.60. -- Amsterdam Newsroom, +31 20 504 5000
